coverage_assessment: Twenty-three captured searches and 537 ordered result headers are preserved with 18 source cards (1 opened body and 17 search-only). Queries cover broad English/French, February date windows, Sonko-affair reporting and leads concerning Bignona, Parcelles Assainies, Place de l’Indépendance, Le Peuple, CUSEMS, electricity tariffs, an official assembly-ban instrument and rights-monitoring reports. One Wolof-oriented query returned French results; no human translation review or substantive Wolof/regional-language corpus was obtained. Coverage is geographically and sectorally uneven, local archives were not comprehensively searched, and this is not exhaustive. E001 has a reported qualitative “thousands” crowd plausibly above 50, but the article does not separate home attendance from the blocked march or state an explicit demand to Senegal’s government; no candidate currently demonstrates both the meeting threshold and a domestic state-directed demand. E001 has arrests=yes and crowd_dispersal=yes; its other five response dimensions and protester violence remain unknown. E002–E008 have no body-level support for dates, meeting counts, demands, protester violence or any state-response dimensions. Their source origins and independence are unverified. Bignona, Dakar, Parcelles and other leads remain unlinked; arrest figures are not attendance. Tariff alert year, locations and execution remain unresolved. S002’s guard failure and S003/S004 Cache misses are not denials. The January 2021 curfew/public-lighting cases are not physically linked to these February leads; no February continuation is coded, and the March aftermath remains outside this unit. This is open-web discovery with unresolved source, language, archive and baseline limits, not a census or fully reviewed dataset.
